method: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first analytical pass. Reopened the adopted Sociology appendix and its choice/admission footnotes, the actual selected stage and major-specific project/thesis entries and the course contents before reconsidering the exact finished UCR selections, contributions, placements and audience text. This is analytical separation by the same AI, not an independent person or live rendering.
findings: The Dutch Sociology track and retained Urban Issues major are confirmed by the adopted 2026–2027 appendix and current September-2026 programme. The first year totals sixty with actual three/five/six/eight-credit units; Year 2 has thirty-six common credits plus twenty-four major credits. The project and thesis use their exact Urban Issues variants. Neither the major parent nor the aggregate elective block is double counted.

The non-exchange third year comprises twelve-credit placement, eighteen genuinely open credits, twelve restricted credits, twelve-credit thesis and six-credit Social Philosophy. The formal I-40 footnote allows two subjects from non-selected majors. Global Migration and Sociology of Work are each six credits and both belong to the non-selected Social Risks major; they coherently extend urban questions. The eighteen open credits allow minor/elective combinations without a named package. Twenty-seven components total 180 uniquely.

Placement entry requires an approved plan and signed contract before starting and at least 336 hours in a relevant organisation. It may be completed part-time during a semester or year; no host is assumed. The thesis is normally Spring and individually empirical, with proposal, article-style report, peer feedback and symposium presentation. The adopted threshold is the full propaedeutic phase PLUS sixty postpropaedeutic credits, not just any 120. Both earlier years meet it. Autumn entry is exceptional and not used.

Migration is offered in Block 2, Work and Social Philosophy in Block 4, and the Urban Issues project in Blocks 3–4. A coherent non-exchange arrangement can place stage/Migration and twelve open credits in Autumn, with thesis/Work/Social Philosophy and six open credits in Spring. Skills 1 precedes 2, and the earlier skills/methods precede Skills 3 with statistics alongside; Project 1 follows. Earlier MTO courses prepare Project 2 while its questionnaire course begins in the same semester. No impossible extra sequential gate is imposed.

All fifty-one interests were reconciled: seventeen eligible generators, twenty-four support-only topics, four illustrations and six outcomes. Removed career-outcome row 9633 from academic-research support while retaining its search role. The urban core and two additional cultural/identity and social-risk priorities remain corroborated by current major descriptions. Neither all three majors nor individual outcomes become compulsory comparator components.

The closest UCR response retains substantial sociology, qualitative inquiry, behavioural statistics, actual survey work, data workflows and econometrics, strengthened by public economics, policy and ethics. The cultural option replaces Renaissance art and an unspecified partner project with social psychology/statistics, retaining actual gender, racial, imperial and Indigenous social histories. Its visible label is bounded to Culture, identity and comparative social history rather than implying a dedicated migration programme. The risk option retains climate, health and environmental governance with policy and causal-data analysis. Eight substitutions serve the prior concepts; qualitative differences and fifty-two-and-a-half, forty-five and seventy-five EC each way pass.

All selected contributions were assessed from actual profile or description evidence, including public-policy and econometrics descriptions. The generic American Century historical-research description received full consideration but does not establish a sociology thesis or more direct thematic contribution than the replacements. The current Leadership-under-pressure course includes an original survey and reliability/quantitative analysis; the old diversity-management name is not carried forward. Four original offering conflicts are repaired. Every actual formal prerequisite and offered term, twenty-four unique courses, four per term, first-year PPD and six advanced courses pass. Advisory progression is considered without invented hard gates.

The source-first content review changes conclusions that title-only comparison would miss: Life Course Sociology concerns health and social determinants, allowing a bounded epidemiological relationship; Causal Techniques concerns ANOVA/correlation/regression/logistic/path models, making behavioural statistics stronger than generic data cleaning; questionnaire construction has a bounded survey counterpart; data workflows fit Skills 3; writing fits Skills 2. Fifteen partial relationships identify important subject/method overlap and scope limits. Twelve gaps preserve dedicated urban study, specialised projects, epistemology, placement, restricted migration/work topics, open space and the individual thesis. Optional research remains outside scheduled credits.

Read all twenty-seven labels, seven selected notes, three concepts, fifteen relationships, twelve gaps and thirty-five selected descriptions against the established renderer mapping and exact input hashes. English title, source links and audience references resolve correctly; the stale OER URL is replaced by current official sources. Unchanged shared descriptions are reused while case-specific course contributions are reassessed. No app/renderer, workbook or enrichment changes, local Shiny/browser launch, screenshots, live modals or final-release approval are claimed.
